profile.campus: Nabiax Julian Camarillo campus, Madrid (3 modules: N1, N2, N3)
address: Calle Julian Camarillo 29, E.1, Planta 3, 28037 Madrid, Spain
profile.reading:
N3 is one of three modules, numbered 1 through 3 on the operator's own site, that make up Nabiax's Julian Camarillo campus at Calle Julian Camarillo 29, Madrid, Spain, near Madrid Barajas airport. The operator's own campus page states the site was inaugurated in phases between 1995 and 2011 and that all three modules are built to Tier III specifications, with 2N generator topology and N+1 chiller and CRAH cooling. The same page gives combined campus totals of 10,000 square meters, about 107,600 square feet, of space, 10 megawatts of current IT power expandable to 15 megawatts, and 29 IT rooms, but does not break any of those figures down by individual module, so no module specific capacity or floor area is attributed to this record. Beyond the module number itself, no public source found in this research distinguishes N3 from N1 or N2 on any technical, capacity, or tenancy basis, and this record does not invent such a distinction.

Nabiax is the operator, and its own company history page states the business began in 2019 when Asterion Industrial Partners acquired 11 data centers from Telefonica for approximately 550 million euros, a valuation industry publication Dgtl Infra separately reported at roughly 18.3 times EBITDA. In May 2021, per that same Dgtl Infra reporting, Telefonica contributed four additional data centers, two in Spain and two in Chile with a combined 9 megawatts of capacity, back to Nabiax in exchange for a 20 percent equity stake, with Asterion and its co-investors retaining the remaining 80 percent. In November 2024, Nabiax's own site and trade press including Data Center Dynamics reported that British investment firm Aermont Capital acquired Nabiax outright from Asterion Industrial Partners and Telefonica, ending Telefonica's remaining minority stake in the business it had originally spun the data centers out of.

Nabiax's own about page states the Julian Camarillo address in Madrid, the same address as this facility, also serves as the company's headquarters. It describes the operator's current Spanish portfolio as 6 data centers organized into 5 centers across 2 campuses, with 26 megawatts of installed IT power across 22,000 square meters company wide, alongside other Spanish locations in Alcala de Henares and Terrassa that this registry tracks as separate facilities from this Madrid campus. The operator states the Julian Camarillo campus runs on 100 percent renewable energy and describes itself as 100 percent carrier neutral, marketing the site to enterprise, telecom, and hyperscale customers as the leading colocation provider in Spain by Nabiax's own framing.

No standby generator rating, utility interconnection figure, or onsite generation figure specific to N3, as distinct from the campus wide totals above, was found in any operator or trade source reviewed. No named tenant for this module was found either. Given the shared address and shared specifications the operator publishes for all three modules, the honest reading of this facility, N3, is as one interchangeable third of a single Tier III campus rather than as a building with a documented identity of its own.

profile.campus_power_note: Nabiax's own Julian Camarillo campus page gives combined totals for all three modules together, 10,000 square meters, 10 megawatts of current IT power expandable to 15 megawatts, and 29 IT rooms. These are campus wide IT capacity figures, not a utility interconnection rating, a standby generator rating, or an onsite generation figure, none of which were found published for this campus. No source found in this research breaks any of these totals down by individual module, N1, N2, or N3, so this registry records the totals at the campus level only and attributes no module specific power or floor area figure to any of the three rows.
